audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 fits: he outranges everything you own (Q 750, W 1000, E 1050) but owns no dash, blink or escape, so every step-up you survive is a kill window.
audit.corrected: Rating kept; the difficulty is now expressed as his range numbers versus his zero mobility.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides read Xerath/Xerath/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill while content win[] and the packet chart both read Diana on all seven rows.
audit.why: Every phases[].why already describes Diana winning that stage, so the sides were the stale layer.
audit.corrected: All seven sides moved to Diana; win[] already Diana everywhere, so no cross-layer disagreement is created and no why needed rewriting.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated ultimate name 'Arcane Barrage'; and nothing stated that Rite of the Arcane immobilizes Xerath himself.
audit.why: Riot's kit names the ultimate Rite of the Arcane and its text reads that Xerath immobilizes himself to gain the barrages — that self-root is the single best window Diana gets.
audit.corrected: Real name used in content.mid and wants.foe[1]; the self-root is now stated in breakdown.carry and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and the packet flagged zero sequencing cues in the whole matchup.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 and 11s at rank 5 — a missed orb is a measurable window, not a vibe.
audit.corrected: Orb 13s/11s, Arcanopulse 9s to 5s, ultimate 130/115/100s, plus 'step up the moment it misses'.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED), and dosFull[2].d / dontsFull[0].d said nothing about their own titles.
audit.why: Bodies must explain the title above them.
audit.corrected: All four replaced with kit-grounded bodies carrying real numbers.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Check it before every step-up. - W Pale Cascade is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb: 13s at rank 1, 11s at rank 5 — his only CC, so step up the moment it misses and you have 11 seconds of free ground. - Arcanopulse is 9s down to 5s; Rite of the Arcane roots him in place for its channel on a 130/115/100s timer.

edits.before: His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Crescent Strike travels 900 to his 750 Arcanopulse — arc it through the wave so he is marked every time he steps up to poke.

edits.before: Q through the wave onto his chest, E the mark, three-hit string, walk — the phase trade he answers after you've left.
edits.after: Pale Cascade shields as the orbs spawn — step up on that window, take the trade, and be gone before Arcanopulse comes in 9s.

edits.before: Xerath whiffs Shocking Orb (Stun) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: A Moonlight mark makes Lunar Rush free; without one it is 22s at rank 1.

edits.before: That is Xerath’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Dashing unmarked spends 22s and lands you inside a 13s Shocking Orb you cannot dodge.

edits.before: Dashing onto an unmarked target with W down — Diana without the reset or the shield is a melee mage donating proximity.
edits.after: Without the Moonlight mark there is no reset, and Xerath simply walks backward casting 750-range Arcanopulse at you.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb from 1050 range, then stacking Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction while you walk it off.

edits.before: Carry through the dive — mark, dash, pull, delete; your R turns their teamfight spacing into a suggestion.
edits.after: Xerath roots himself in place to cast Rite of the Arcane — that is your window to dash on him and finish it.

edits.before: Level 6 makes this even more one-sided: Moonfall extends your engage range significantly, letting you punish him even if he tries to poke from a safer distance. His own ultimate, Arcane Barrage, does huge damage but he has to commit to landing all three casts, which leaves him extremely exposed if you're already in range. Keep closing distance every chance you get and don't let him free-cast from a safe zone.
edits.after: Level 6 makes this even more one-sided: Moonfall extends your engage range significantly, letting you punish him even if he tries to poke from a safer distance. His own ultimate, Rite of the Arcane, does huge damage but he immobilizes himself for its duration, which leaves him extremely exposed if you're already in range. Keep closing distance every chance you get and don't let him free-cast from a safe zone.

edits.before: Use Arcane Barrage to zone your engage attempts
edits.after: Use Rite of the Arcane to zone your engage attempts

notes: 'Arcane Barrage' was a fabricated ultimate name in content.mid and wants.foe[1]; Riot's kit calls it Rite of the Arcane. All seven full-layer sides were stale against content win[] and the packet chart and were aligned to Diana with the whys already matching. Whether Diana's Moonfall pull actually interrupts Rite of the Arcane is not stated in Riot's text (only the derived 'channel' flag suggests it), so it was not asserted — breakdown.carry says only that he is rooted in place while casting. tradeGood/tradeBad left alone: still generic, but nothing further in Xerath's kit to ground them without inventing.
